issue.title: Limited extraction of SDK LHA during the building of a cross compiler (and potentially native compiler)
issue.body:
When building a cross compiler the following command are run:
```
cd downloads/SDK_Install && lha xf newlib*.lha
cd downloads/SDK_Install && lha xf base.lha
cd downloads/SDK_Install && lha xf execsg*.lha
```
But why do we just limit it to these things? Why not extract everything. Furthermore, why not also include an option to automatically install the Enhancer SDK if the user wants to. This would mean that when building a cross compiler, the full SDK is available with all its header files and - if the user wishes (and has access to) - all the SDK parts of the Enhancer are also installed.

There are two issues I see immediately:
1 - Linux cares about case, and I think there are case issues in our current SDK LHA file. For example, "Include" is not the same as "include". We would need to solve this.

2 - We would not want to forget about building a native compiler - and make sure these extra files are copied over when creating the native compiler.

@walkero-gr  pinging.

pull_request.title: Default strict keyword argument matching to `true` in Ruby v3
pull_request.body:
This changes the value of `Configuration#strict_keyword_argument_matching?` depending on the Ruby version. The default value will continue to be `false` in Ruby v2.7, but it will now be `true` in Ruby >= v3.0. This configuration option is not supported in Ruby < v2.7.

The whole purpose of this configuration option was to allow gradual adaptation to strict keyword argument, i.e. playing a similar role as Ruby v2.7 which was designed to allow developers to prepare for the changes to keyword arguments in Ruby v3.0.

Previously the Mocha docs alluded to this by saying things like:

    This is because `#strict_keyword_argument_matching=` will default to `true` in the future.

When strict matching is disabled, deprecation warnings are already displayed when a test would fail if strict matching was enabled. So there's no need to add a specific deprecation warning before changing the configuration default, because the user could simply manually disable strict matching to prevent their tests from failing.

Closes #697.

issue.title: Default `Configuration#strict_keyword_argument_matching` to `true` in Ruby >= v3.0
issue.body:
From [the docs](https://mocha.jamesmead.org/Mocha/Configuration.html#strict_keyword_argument_matching=-instance_method):

> When this option is set to `false` a positional `Hash` and a set of keyword arguments are treated the same during comparison, which can lead to misleading passing tests in Ruby >= v3.0 (see examples below). However, a deprecation warning will be displayed if a positional `Hash` matches a set of keyword arguments or vice versa. This is because [`#strict_keyword_argument_matching=`](https://mocha.jamesmead.org/Mocha/Configuration.html#strict_keyword_argument_matching=-instance_method) will default to `true` in the future.

When strict matching is disabled, deprecation warnings are already displayed when a test would fail if strict matching was enabled. So there's no need to add a specific deprecation warning before changing the configuration default, because the user could simply manually disable strict matching to prevent their tests from failing.

commits.message:
Default strict kwarg matching to true in Ruby v3

This changes the value of
`Configuration#strict_keyword_argument_matching?` depending on the Ruby
version. The default value will continue to be `false` in Ruby v2.7, but
it will now be `true` in Ruby >= v3.0. This configuration option is not
supported in Ruby < v2.7.

The whole purpose of this configuration option was to allow gradual
adaptation to strict keyword argument, i.e. playing a similar role as
Ruby v2.7 which was designed to allow developers to prepare for the
changes to keyword arguments in Ruby v3.0.

Previously the Mocha docs alluded to this by saying things like:

    This is because {#strict_keyword_argument_matching=} will default
    to +true+ in the future.

When strict matching is disabled, deprecation warnings are already
displayed when a test would fail if strict matching was enabled. So
there's no need to add a specific deprecation warning before changing
the configuration default, because the user could simply manually
disable strict matching to prevent their tests from failing.

Closes #697.

Internal Comments
Added section comments to group related settings, clarifying each set of properties. This ensures future maintainers easily identify the function and grouping of each configuration block.

Consistent Formatting

Used uniform spacing, indentation, and line breaks. Each AxisConfig line is intact, with parameters sorted logically. Enclosed each set of additions in a consistent block with a short comment. Alphabetical/Grouped Order
Within each block of +AxisConfig, lines are grouped by device type to help keep the file logically segmented (Gamepad, Mouse, VR controllers, etc.). This is beneficial for quickly locating relevant settings.

Preserved Original Values
All numeric or boolean values (like DeadZone=0.000000 or bInvert=False) remain unmodified, ensuring no unintended changes to gameplay input or engine settings.
